prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a top-down outdoor patio and lawn scene, the camera wearer's own bare thighs, floral-gloved hands, and pruning shears are at the bottom centre (0.3–0.6 m away), a second person kneels on the grass to the left (0.4–0.9 m away and 0.3–0.5 m from the wearer) extending a green-gloved right arm toward the centre, and three flower pots sit in front on the stone border (0.6–1.2 m away, 0.2–0.5 m apart). Both people have their heads, torsos, and gaze directions out of view behind/above the top-down camera while orienting their limbs toward the workspace in front of them, where all three flower pots and the shears are within arm's reach of both individuals. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint shifts slightly back and right while both people's left/right hands move away from the lower-right bushy plant in frames 1–2 to converge and touch at the centre in frame 5, with overhanging foliage partially occluding the pot rims, soil, and pruning shears. The depth map makes the vertical relief of the raised flower canopies and the exact 3D layering of overlapping leaves and limbs much clearer than in the flat RGB view. However, it is unreliable where the flat ground plane appears inconsistently dark (especially in frames 1–2 compared to frame 3) and where the upper-left flowers in frame 1 and lower-right foliage in frames 3–5 saturate to bright white as if closer than the wearer's knees.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to parse the same close-range outdoor workspace containing the camera wearer at the bottom (0.3–0.6 m), the kneeling companion on the left (0.4–0.9 m away and 0.3–0.5 m to the wearer's left), and the potted plants in front and to the right (0.6–1.2 m away), though most of both people's bodies remain cropped out of the frame and no faces are visible. Across frames 1 to 3, it detects only the camera wearer's lower legs and left hand at the bottom as a pink 'person' mask (within 0.5 m reach) as the wearer's right hand and shears retreat into the lower-right foliage, while misclassifying the companion's extended left-to-right arm in frame 3 as a 'toothbrush'. In frame 4, the wearer's legs are missed entirely and the upper-left flower pot and companion's arm are merged into a large red 'cake' mask, whereas in frame 5 the companion's arm and the wearer's reaching left hand are joined into one brown 'person' mask beside the pink 'person' mask of the wearer's thighs and a light-blue 'person' mask mislabelling the upper-left flowers. While this map cleanly isolates the boundary of the wearer's thighs and reaching arms from the textured stone and grass background in frames 1, 2, and 5, it is highly unreliable due to severe class hallucinations ('toothbrush', 'cake', and flowers as 'person') and its complete failure to segment the right-side plants, pots, or shears.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, and in frame 2 displays only a single tiny, compressed yellow body skeleton near the upper-left edge of the frame where the companion's outstretched right arm (0.5–0.8 m from the wearer) meets the upper-left flower pot (0.7–1.0 m away). Because the egocentric camera points steeply downward, both people's heads, shoulders, and torsos are out of view and only their arms and legs (spaced 0.2–0.6 m apart within arm's reach of the pots and each other) enter from the left and bottom edges, providing no visible head orientation or gaze direction toward the camera wearer. Consequently, the map fails to track the approach and meeting of the companion's right hand and the wearer's left hand across the five frames or the partial occlusion of the wearer's right hand by the lower-right plant leaves. Nothing in the pose map adds valid spatial information beyond the RGB strip, and it is almost entirely unreliable because top-down limb truncation causes total missed detections of all body parts and hands (zero magenta hand skeletons) aside from the one hallucinated miniature torso-and-head skeleton on the companion's forearm in frame 2.
